summary: Tested configurable template-level PF (pf_config) on LOCAL DB. Backend: new suite tests/test_payslip_pf_config.py 25/25 PASS. It covers: engine at 30/25/24/20/0 payable days (PF 3000/3000/2880/2400/0; 24 days gives Basic 16000, DA 8000, HRA 5600, Phone 2400, Food 1600, Special 1600, gross 35200, net 31820; 30 days gives deductions 3500, net 40500); the 10%/2500 variant; disabled gives PF 0; legacy (no pf_config) still gives 1800; a 42000 vs 44000 mismatch raises a 400 reconciliation error and a 0.5 difference is allowed; a synthetic 'PF' line is added when the template has no PF component; extra pay is kept out of the PF base; ROUND_HALF_UP. API: create with a valid pf_config is stored; pct 0/150/'abc', max 0, empty components, unknown component, deduction component and PF component all give 400; removing DA via PUT gives 400 (also 400 when the stale pf_config is resent), and fixing the selection gives 200; a PUT with only pf_config updates it and keeps the components; a legacy template is untouched by an unrelated PUT. Preview and generate for a TEST_PF_ employee give the same PF and net (payable 4 days with no attendance, PF 480). After confirming, regenerate skips the slip and it stays unchanged. Frontend: the full PF Configuration flow passes: section and legacy note shown, validation toasts work, create → reopen keeps 12/3000/Basic+DA, removing the DA row shows the red warning and blocks saving with a toast, 'remove them from PF' clears it and the save then succeeds. All TEST_PF_ data was hard-deleted (5 templates, 1 assignment, 1 payslip, 14 audits, 3 employees); the payslip collections and employees are back to 0.

minor.issue: pf_config: null is silently ignored (the _validate_pf_config(None) branch returns None and nothing is $unset). Once a template is on the new model it can never go back to legacy PF.

Name mismatch: the backend _pf_eligible_names uses the untrimmed c['name'], but the frontend uses name.trim() for eligibility and the pf_config component list. A component named 'Basic ' (trailing space) passes the UI check and then gets a 400 'not found' from the backend. Trim component names on save (frontend or _validate_components).

ui_bugs.issue: On a legacy template, ticking then unticking 'PF Enabled' sets pfConfig to {enabled:false} and removes the legacy note. Saving then sends pf_config {enabled:false}, which silently turns PF off entirely (PF = 0) for a template that had a legacy PF component. There is no way back to legacy in the UI. Suggest: unticking on a template that had no pf_config should reset pfConfig to null, or add a clear 'Use legacy PF' option.

action_items: TemplateForm: unticking PF Enabled on a template with no saved pf_config should go back to legacy (pfConfig=null) and not save {enabled:false}
Optional: let PUT pf_config:null $unset pf_config so a template can return to legacy
Trim component names (and pf_config component names) on save so frontend and backend eligibility agree
critical_code_review_comments: The earning-total vs Monthly Gross check only runs at preview/generate time (per assignment). A template whose earnings do not sum to the gross (for example 70% total) saves without any warning and only fails during generation, where it shows as a per-employee error. That is acceptable by design, but a hint in the UI would help.
Frontend eligibility regex /pf|provident|gratuity/ matches backend _is_pf/_is_gratuity. OK.
payslip_module.py is 919 lines (over 700). Consider splitting the engine (compute_payslip) into its own module.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the requested flows; 1 UX edge-case bug

test_credentials: admin/pass123 works on the LOCAL DB (test_credentials.md lists HrAdmin@2109, which fails locally). The payslip 6-digit code 082026 must be verified via POST /api/payslip-security/verify (with a browser User-Agent) before any /api/payslips* call.
